problem: Multi-hop KGQA systems must balance answer accuracy against strict latency and token-cost targets while preserving provenance; static k-hop expansion and 'think-longer' prompting over-retrieve, inflate context, and give unpredictable runtime.
method: CLAUSE treats context construction as a sequential decision process over the KG and learns it with Lagrangian-Constrained Multi-Agent PPO (LC-MAPPO). Three agents - Subgraph Architect, Path Navigator, Context Curator - jointly decide what to expand, which paths to follow/backtrack, which evidence to keep, and when to stop, subject to per-query budgets on edge edits, interaction steps, and selected tokens; budgets/prices are exposed at inference without retraining.
key_assumptions: Context construction can be modeled as an MDP over the symbolic KG state.
Compact, provenance-preserving context is better than large fixed-k-hop expansion.
Latency and token cost can be exposed as per-query budgets/prices.
Compact neural scorers can prioritize entities, relations, and neighborhoods.
main_contribution: An agentic neuro-symbolic KGQA framework with the LC-MAPPO constrained multi-agent RL algorithm that jointly optimizes subgraph construction, path discovery, and evidence curation under per-query resource budgets, yielding compact contexts and predictable runtime.
results: Across HotpotQA, MetaQA, and FactKG, CLAUSE yields higher EM@1 while reducing subgraph growth and end-to-end latency at equal or lower token budgets. On MetaQA-2-hop, relative to GraphRAG, it achieves +39.3 EM@1 with 18.6% lower latency and 40.9% lower edge growth.
limitations: Reports only MetaQA-2-hop headline improvement; deeper-hop behavior not emphasized in the abstract.
Optimizes context selection, not the language model's training supervision.
Requires an RL training pipeline for the agent policies.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: CLAUSE trains the context-selection policy (agents) with constrained RL under latency/token budgets; it does not change the reader model's training supervision, does not compare triple-only vs context-enriched supervision, has no adaptive one-hop repair loop, and does not train only on shallow hops to test transfer to deeper hops. The proposed idea is training-time supervision enrichment rather than inference-time context engineering.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap high: both are about constructing a local subgraph of KG triples as context for multi-hop QA. Method overlap moderate-high: both use RL and subgraph construction, but the RL target differs (context policy vs the answering model) and CLAUSE is inference-time. Evaluation overlap high: shared MetaQA benchmark, but CLAUSE reports EM@1 under token budgets, whereas the idea compares training regimes and hop depths.
